official_sources.title: IETF HTTP Content-Digest and Repr-Digest integrity fields
official_sources.finding: RFC 9530 distinguishes a digest of actual HTTP message content from a digest of the selected representation, including partial-range cases where Content-Digest and Repr-Digest can legitimately differ.
official_sources.limitation: Digest fields prove integrity only for the defined byte scope; they do not authenticate the publisher or prove that the raster is the intended official product.

official_sources.title: HTTP strong validators, range requests and If-Range
official_sources.finding: RFC 9110 distinguishes strong and weak validators; strong validators support range requests and If-Range can force a full current representation when the validator no longer matches.
official_sources.limitation: An ETag is opaque and is not necessarily a content hash; weak validators are insufficient for byte-identical reconstruction.

official_sources.title: NIST FIPS 180-4 Secure Hash Standard
official_sources.authority: National Institute of Standards and Technology
official_sources.finding: FIPS 180-4 specifies SHA-256 as a secure hash algorithm producing a 256-bit message digest from the complete input message.
official_sources.limitation: A digest must be computed over the exact complete byte stream; hashing decoded pixels or a partial download identifies a different object.

official_sources.title: JSON Canonicalization Scheme for invariant manifests
official_sources.finding: RFC 8785 defines canonical JSON using I-JSON constraints, deterministic property sorting, strict primitive serialization, UTF-8 output and no inter-token whitespace so hashing and signing are repeatable.
official_sources.limitation: JCS accepts only IEEE-754-compatible JSON numbers; large integers or exact decimal identifiers should be encoded as strings when precision could be lost.

official_sources.title: HTTP Message Signatures over selected components
official_sources.finding: RFC 9421 defines strict canonicalization and detached signatures over selected HTTP components and can cover digest fields, validators, target URI and other provenance metadata.
official_sources.limitation: A valid signature is only as trustworthy as its key policy and covered-component selection; content bytes require a covered digest field.

official_sources.title: OGC Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF HTTP range conformance
official_sources.finding: The OGC COG standard requires HTTP byte-range support for cloud-served TIFF files and defines conformance tests for retrieving only needed file fragments.
official_sources.limitation: Range support improves access efficiency but does not alone prove that separate ranges came from one immutable representation.

official_sources.title: GDAL /vsicurl range access, cache and retry behavior
official_sources.finding: GDAL /vsicurl relies on HTTP range requests, keeps a global downloaded-content cache, and exposes retry and cache controls that can affect which remote bytes are reused during a process.
official_sources.limitation: Cached chunks can outlive a file handle; a remote-object version change during one process can mix stale and fresh bytes unless validators and cache policy are bound.

official_sources.title: STAC File Info extension size and checksum metadata
official_sources.finding: The stable STAC File Info extension defines file-related asset metadata including byte size and checksum, supporting immutable asset identity in catalog manifests.
official_sources.limitation: Catalog metadata must be independently verified against downloaded bytes and pinned to a specific STAC item, collection and extension version.
